newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK markets seen welcoming easier IPO flow.
newsitem.headline: HK markets seen welcoming easier IPO flow.

text.p: Strong demand for new issues has caused tightness in Hong Kong's money market but a request by the Hong Kong Monetary Authory to ease the IPO flow should give both the money and IPO markets a breather, analysts said.
From Monday, the HKMA will introduce a new Real Time Gross Settlement System (RTGS) requiring banks to make real time settlements instead of daily settlements.
In order to relieve money market tightness around the launch it has asked merchant banks to delay upcoming new issues, analysts said.

"It is considered to be good for IPOs," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities. "It is good because the market can have a bit of time to digest recent new listings, and the delay is just a very short period of time."

Under the RTGS, banks can use Exchange Fund bills and notes to obtain interest free intraday liquidity by carrying out intraday repurchase transactions with the HKMA. Banks would make real-time settlements instead of daily settlements and a heavy IPO schedule could complicate its launch, traders said.
"We expressed our wishes to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange that the IPO schedule will not be so tight during the first week of implementation of the RTGS," an HKMA spokesman said.
In late November the HKMA had to inject about HK$3.0 billion into the banking system to soothe market tightness.

"Market liquidity was tight at the end of the month due to month-end corporate demand, strong equities-related demand and ahead of the implementation of a new settlement system," said one money dealer at a European bank.
Recent heavily subscribed IPOs include Jackin International Holdings Ltd, Mirabell International Holdings Ltd and Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd.

Data storage products maker Jackin International's 90.75 million share IPO was 257.9 times subscribed and shoe retailer Mirabell International drew a subscription level of 190.5 times for its 60 million share offering.
The public portion of China property concern Nam Fong International's 340 million share issue was 165.6 times subscribed.

"The recent high oversubscription rates for IPOs have frozen up quite a big sum of money, especially when a few IPOs are launched at the same time," said Patrick Chia, research manager of China Everbright Securities.

Guangdong Tannery Ltd, the leather unit of Guangdong Investment Ltd offered 110 million shares last week at HK$1.03 per share. Analysts expect the offering, which closed on Friday, to be more than 200 times subscribed. Dealing in the shares is due to begin on December 16.

A 125 million share offering by cable maker and exporter Solartech International Holdings last week at HK$1.20 per share was expected to draw a subscription level of 60 to 70 times, analysts said. Solartech is due to begin trading on December 12.
Analysts said there were still about four or five new issues expected to be launched by the end of December. They said it was hard to say how many would be affected by the HKMA's request.

"Even though we believe market sentiment will remain positive (in 1997), some companies may rush to list by the end of the year since there is still an element of uncertainty about (market) sentiment in 1997," said one analyst.

Electrical cable maker Perennial International Ltd is expected to kick off an IPO this coming week and KP Holdings, a plastic component maker, is expected to offer shares later this month. Plywood maker Tai Fu International Holdings is expected to launch a HK$200 million offering between December 11 and 16.

Analysts expect Chinese state-owned medicine maker Shangdong Xinhua Pharmaceutical Co to launch a roadshow soon for a HK$300 million H-share issue and satellite firm APT Satellite Holdings Ltd is expected to raise US$250 million in a December listing.
